title: Minimax Precision on a Lattice When the Spillover Direction Is Unknown
banked_reason: D0.5 typed achieved subfield below fixed field floor; paper_score_ceiling 7.0 < 7.4 and salvageable=false. Independent main validity gate confirms sound narrow rate frontier and no bounded same-topic field lift.
proof_attempt_summary: for the hidden global axis and (r+1)/N for the known-axis oracle, including the persistence of the quadratic penalty after post-assignment axis disclosure and an O(N) attainer. Math and decision panels passed; final typed novelty review and independent main validity gate judged the package subfield, below the fixed field floor, because of narrow geometry and limited quantitative impact. Exact constants, normalized limits, and scalable constant-optimal procedures remain open; formalization was not entered and no Lean module was generated.
tldr: On a labeled square torus with arbitrary bounded fixed response tables and one globally shared horizontal or vertical spillover axis, minimax mean squared error has uniform order \((r+1)/N\) when the axis is known before design choice and \((r+1)^2/N\) when it is hidden through assignment. The quadratic order persists even if the axis is disclosed before analysis. Independent square-cluster assignment and a total clipped endpoint rule attain the unknown-axis order, and a legal many-coordinate fixed-schedule prior supplies the converse for every outcome-independent law and every randomized original-record estimator. The oracle is an evaluated lattice specialization of the published ANI/GATE minimax problem, with an exact fixed-axis conflict-graph starting optimization. Sharp normalized constants, their limits, and scalable constant-optimal procedures remain open.
gap: Unknown-interference inference already exists: Wang, Samii, Chang, and Aronow target a design-marginalized spatial effect, while Yu, Airoldi, Borgs, and Chayes target the universal-treatment contrast under additive responses and baseline information \cite{WangSamiiChangAronow2025UnknownSpatial,YuAiroldiBorgsChayes2022UnknownNetwork}. Neither evaluates the all-design, all-original-record minimax precision of arbitrary fixed tables over one globally exclusive directional menu. Known-network minimax theory and spatial linear-estimator theory also leave this evaluation unresolved.
fill: The principal theorem evaluates \(R_A\), \(R\), and \(R_{\mathrm{post}}\) uniformly with an explicit original-record attainer, a legal one-shared-axis fixed-schedule converse, and declared arithmetic cost. The rate separation isolates the value of predesign geometry information. The open sharp-efficiency question concerns the constants not supplied by the rate argument.
